stem:
Choose the best topic sentence to fill the blank.

__________. A short walk after meals helps control blood sugar. Taking the stairs instead of the elevator makes the heart stronger. Even ten minutes of stretching can ease a stiff back.
choices: Elevators in government offices are often crowded.
Doctors say that sugar is bad for the heart.
Small amounts of exercise can improve health.
Many people have no time to go to the gym.
answer: Small amounts of exercise can improve health.
hints: Look at what the three sentences after the blank have in common.
Each sentence names a small activity and a health benefit. Put that shared idea into a few words.
Pick the choice that covers all three activities and their benefits, not one that borrows a single word from one sentence.

solution.methodName: Find the sentence that covers all the others

steps.action: Read the details: a short walk, taking the stairs, ten minutes of stretching.
steps.why: These are all small, easy kinds of exercise.

steps.action: Note what each one does: controls blood sugar, makes the heart stronger, eases a stiff back.
Combine the two: small amounts of exercise improve health.
steps.why: A topic sentence states the idea that all the details support.

steps.action: Check the choices against this idea. Only one covers all three details.
The best topic sentence is "Small amounts of exercise can improve health."

trapNotes.Elevators in government offices are ofte: Elevators appear in only one detail, and only as something to avoid. The paragraph is about exercise and health, not crowded elevators.
trapNotes.Doctors say that sugar is bad for the he: It borrows "sugar" and "heart" from the details but mixes them up. The paragraph is about exercise, not about sugar.
trapNotes.Many people have no time to go to the gy: The paragraph never talks about lack of time. Its details are about the health benefits of small exercises.
